datasets.name: Optical image data (Google Earth)
datasets.verbatim: The remote sensing data used in this study include the optical image data (downloaded from Google Earth) and the global Digital Elevation Model (DEM).

datasets.name: Landslide inventory (manually interpreted)
datasets.source: Authors' own manual interpretation and field investigation
datasets.verbatim: In our study, the existing landslide was manually interpreted in remote sensing images downloaded from Google Earth and validated by field investigation from October to December 2022 (Fig. 6).

methods.name: Trans-VGG (Transformer-improved VGG network)
methods.summary: A hybrid deep learning model that integrates a VGG-based convolutional neural network for local feature extraction with a multi-head attention module for global feature dependency modeling. It takes stacked spectral (RGB) and non-spectral (elevation, slope, PCA) data as 1D inputs to perform pixel-based landslide classification.
methods.verbatim: The code and data used in this study can be found at https://github.com/JJJay11/Trans-VGG-for-Landslide-Detection and https://zenodo.org/records/12577262.

data_links.name: Experiment dataset for landslide detection study

code_links.name: Trans-VGG code for landslide detection
code_links.summary: Custom code implementing a Trans-VGG model for landslide detection, run in a Python 3.6.5 environment and shared alongside the data.

availability.author_statement: Full availability statement (through supplementary material), with description and referencing of artifacts (no shared links).

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and experiment dataset are linked via Zenodo, and input datasets are accessible through public providers like USGS EarthExplorer. The custom Trans-VGG code is available via a persistent GitHub repository link.
